text: T-SQL Development already covered writing SQL. This course doesn't re-teach any of that — every skill gets redirected toward keeping the database running, secure, fast, and recoverable.

A developer's SQL answers "how do I get the data I need?" A DBA's job starts after that query already works — does it run fast enough, is the right person allowed to see it, what happens if the server goes down.
This course follows Microsoft's DP-300 blueprint, and its section lengths deliberately mirror the real exam weighting across platform resources, security, monitoring, automation, and HA/DR.

Sixteen chapters, one arc: get an environment running, lock it down, know when something's wrong, automate the routine work, migrate in, back it up, survive an outage. Next up: on-prem SQL Server versus Azure SQL.
